comparison: Both evaluations support the structural determination work (C7, C39-C47, C124-C125). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of resolution, model completeness, and methodology. Peer reviewers acknowledge the structure as 'well done' and 'high quality,' validating it against previous OSCA structures. Strong agreement on structural claims.

Both support structural comparison claims (C48-C53). OpenEval details RMSD values and pore profile analysis. Peer reviewers validate the structure against previous OSCA cryo-EM structures. Agreement on structural conservation and closed state interpretation.

Both support lipid density observations (C54-C57, C126). OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from cryo-EM and MD simulations. Peer reviewers do not specifically challenge these structural observations. Agreement on lipid positioning in the structure.

Both support structural comparisons with previous OSCA3.1 structures (C58-C64). OpenEval details conformational differences and improved resolution. Peer reviewers validate the structure against previous work. Agreement on the 'extended' state designation.

Perfect agreement on AH structural conservation claims (C65-C70). OpenEval provides detailed structural analysis and functional context. Peer reviewers accept this as established background for functional studies. Both support the AH conservation and its role in mechanosensation.

Strong agreement on AH mutation effects on poke responses (C71-C82, C127). OpenEval finds data well-supported with adequate sample sizes. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'mutations in the AH of OSCA1.2 decrease the sensitivity to poking stimulus' and accept the methodology as solid. Both support the selective disruption of poke responses.

Strong agreement on selective effects of AH mutations (C83-C93, C132). OpenEval emphasizes the key finding that stretch responses are preserved. Peer reviewers note 'these mutations have similar stretch activated currents to the WT' and accept this demonstrates different mechanisms for poke vs stretch. Both support the selective uncoupling.

Both evaluate the AH sequence swap control experiment (C94, C130). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting the negative result is informative. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that 'the study falls short of explaining why OSCA3.1 does not respond efficiently to poke stimuli.' Disagreement on interpretation completeness.

Both rate OSCA3.1 poke activation as UNCERTAIN (C95-C101). OpenEval cites low response rate (3/10) and small sample size as limiting conclusions. Peer reviewers note the finding but express concern about incomplete mechanistic explanation for OSCA3.1's poor poke response. Agreement on uncertainty, though for slightly different reasons.

Both support the BLD chimera experiment results (C102-C108, C129, C137). OpenEval notes the nuanced conclusion that BLD has minimal effect on poke but may play a modulatory role. Peer reviewers do not challenge the experimental findings. Agreement that the data is sound, though the BLD's role is complex.

Strong agreement on fenestration residue mutations (C115-C123, C128, C140-C142). OpenEval emphasizes dramatic loss of poke responsiveness (1/20 cells) with preserved stretch activation. Peer reviewers accept this as part of demonstrating 'poke and stretch responses likely use different mechanisms.' Both support the selective impairment finding.

Both address lipid-interacting residues. OpenEval R11 focuses on functional effects of mutations (C115-C123), while Peer R10 addresses the structural observation of these residues (C116-C117). Both support the identification and importance of these residues, though evaluating different aspects.

Strong agreement on main conclusions about differential mechanosensing (C9-C12, C37-C38, C148-C149, C151, C153-C154). OpenEval synthesizes findings showing selective disruption across two mutation sets. Peer reviewers state 'the findings on OSCA1.2 will be of interest' and accept the demonstration of different mechanisms. Both support the functional diversity interpretation.

Both support the core conclusion about different mechanisms (C9, C148-C149). OpenEval synthesizes the overall findings. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'the authors use solid methodology to show that poke and stretch responses likely use different mechanisms.' Strong agreement on this key conclusion.

OpenEval evaluates evolutionary coupling and chimera studies from cited work (C133-C136) as SUPPORTED context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific cited claims, though peer reviewers discuss BLD chimera results elsewhere.

OpenEval rates mechanistic model for lipid interactions (C138-C146) as UNCERTAIN, noting proposals are speculative and require further testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these mechanistic hypotheses.
OpenEval evaluates the caveat about lipid composition differences (C147) as SUPPORTED background information. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific contextual claim.
OpenEval evaluates the PIEZO2 comparison (C150) as SUPPORTED context for broader significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific comparative claim.
OpenEval evaluates OSCA-TMEM16 structural similarities (C152) as SUPPORTED but speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific comparative structural claim.
